changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retailers with stores and online (lead with this to COO and store-ops buyers): "One system for the tills and the website. Return an online order at any till: the store sees the order, refunds the original payment and updates the same customer record, so loyalty works everywhere. One customer, one basket." Show this flow live in the demo; don't just describe it. Don't say "unified commerce," "point of sale" or "in-person payments" with store teams. Say "tills." Before using this line, confirm with Solutions that the live cross-channel till return can actually be demoed. The interview leaves that open.
changes.why: The buyer dismissed our M3 line as "that's a diagram," asked step by step how a return works at the till and asked to see it live, and her trigger was an online order the store couldn't see and a loyalty program split across channels, so the line has to be the concrete flow in her own words.

changes.change: For multi-store retail rollouts: "One contract, one team accountable, from the website to the last till. No two vendors pointing at each other." Back it with a dated rollout plan that says who installs, who is on site on a Saturday and what happens to the old tills. Name the people on our side who have done store rollouts. If a partner does the installs, present it as part of our contract with us accountable end to end. Never present it as "we'd bring in a partner."
changes.why: The decider said "I don't want two vendors pointing at each other," our "we'd bring in a partner" answer ended the questioning, and she asked for a rollout plan with who installs, while Adyen won with a retail rollout team on one contract.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers: "Talk to a retailer like you. We'll set up a call this week with someone running our tills and website together." Offer a callable peer reference the buyer would recognize, not a case study.
changes.why: The decider asked "can I talk to them?", we couldn't set up a call in time and sent a case study instead, and Adyen named retailers she knew.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Don't lead with the developer and checkout message when the deal's pain is in the stores and the COO or store-ops team owns it. Keep it for the CTO and ecommerce track, and run a separate store-ops track built on operational outcomes, one accountable vendor and rollout risk.
changes.why: Our checkout demo landed only with the ecommerce lead and the CTO, who ran the RFP, while the COO decided, 11 of the 14 questions were about stores, and the decision meeting was with her store team.
